label: Q01
question: What licence applies to the sonobuoy detection data?
context: marmam-app's LICENSE (MIT) covers the app code, not the data. The release refuses license = unknown without this question open. Checked 2026-09-27: marmam-app's LICENSE is MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2024 PSTAT197-F23' (the UCSB data-science capstone that built the app), and grants rights over 'this software and associated documentation files'. The class did not collect the data, so it cannot license them; the lab must name the data licence.

label: Q03
question: Confirm the curator: the Scripps Whale Acoustics Lab (provider sio), PI Simone Baumann-Pickering?
context: Inferred from the marmam-app co-author list.
proposed_answer: provider = sio, dataset = cetacean-sonobuoy, PIs Baumann-Pickering and Hildebrand.

label: Q04
question: Are Date and Hour in UTC?
context: Sonobuoy recordings are named by their start time (e.g. CC0808SB02_0815213000), usually UTC; nothing in the sheet says so.
proposed_answer: UTC (our reading, to be confirmed). In the release (v2026.09.11), 58 sampled deployments each start 0-1 h before (never 7-8 h off) the CTD/bottle/net sample at the same station on the same cruise, whose times are UTC; this holds on summer and winter cruises alike. Two recording file names shown in marmam-app (CC0808SB02_0815213000, CC0711-SB13-071110-201000) also fall in the sheet's own hours for those buoys.

label: Q05
question: What do the * and ** markers on Quality mean, and what is 'High/Poor'?
context: Quality is published verbatim (trimmed, lower-cased) as measurement_qual; a consumer cannot filter on a grade whose meaning is unknown. First render (2026-09-27): the ** grade (844 hours, all 2004-2007) co-occurs with ** on the background scale in 843 of them, and every one carries the comment 'static takes over 5min 11sec (or 7min 48sec) into each 10min file'. The single * (77 hours, 60 on CC1004MF) carries 'just static ... questionable viability'. 'high/poor' is one hour.
proposed_answer: '**' = static takes over part-way through each 10-min file, so only its first part was usable; '*' = questionable viability, mostly static. Kept verbatim in measurement_qual.

label: Q06
question: CC Line is rounded (83 for 83.3, 87 for 86.7, ...). Is the reverse mapping right, and what are lines 76, 82, 86 and 92?
context: Positions come from line/station, so a wrong line puts the deployment in the wrong place.

label: Q07
question: What do 'Hour spans' and 'Start/End' record?
context: Neither is published until defined. First render (2026-09-27): e.g. CC0407DSJ_SB03 'starts 18:28:54' has hour span 4 (files at :28, :38, :48, :58), then 6 for the full hour, then 4 for 'ends 20:39:59'; CC0604_SB08 'starts 18:36:56' = 3 and 'ends 20:45:27' = 5. Some cruises reach 7-9 per hour (shorter files).
proposed_answer: Hour spans = the number of sound files (normally 10-min, so 6 = a full hour) that fall in the analysed hour; Start/End = the clock time the recording starts or ends inside the first or last hour. Together they give the effort actually scanned in each hour.

label: Q08
question: 154 hours are 'adhoc only'. Were they scanned systematically for all three species?
context: An absence is only an absence if the hour was scanned for the species.
proposed_answer: Kept as scan samples but given no acoustic_presence obs (neither 1 nor 0).

label: Q09
question: 'Spp. Detected' disagrees with the call-type flags on a few hours (e.g. CC1207OS 'Blue' with Blue B = Blue D = 0). Which is right?
context: The ingest counts how many hours disagree per species and reports them.
proposed_answer: The call-type flags are authoritative; the free-text column is kept for audit only.

label: Q10
question: 141 hours have no line/station (e.g. CC1104SH SB60, 'deployed somewhere between 77/70 and San Diego'). Are positions available?
context: Without a position the hour has no grid cell or hex. First render (2026-09-27): 128 of the 141 hours are the 39 DIFAR deployments of CC1004MF (cruise 2010-04-31FN), which has no CTD casts in the release but has swfsc_ichthyo tows and CUFES samples; the first 13 deployments checked each have a track point within 60 min (nearest 0-58 min), along lines 91.7 and 95.0.
proposed_answer: Position each no-station deployment at the nearest-in-time point of its own cruise's track in the release (net tows, CUFES), within 60 min, and flag it as a ship position, not a station.

label: Q11
question: What do the background codes mean (Sarah's scale; Types of Background 1,2,3,A,B)?
context: Not published until defined. First render (2026-09-27): Sarah's scale reads as an ordinal amount of background noise (bit < lots < tons, with ranges such as 'bit to lots'); its ** marker is the same flag as on Quality (Q05). The Types of Background codes (1, 2, 3, A, B, and 'dark <30Hz') are still undefined.

label: Q13
question: Were blue whale calls scored on the July 2009 cruise (CC0907MA)?
context: First render (2026-09-27): 62 systematically scanned hours on CC0907MA and none flags a blue whale call (Spp. Detected agrees), which pulls blue whale 2009 to 4 of 303 hours (1.3%) against 8-36% in other years. Blue whales are usually heard on summer cruises (CC0808NH: 67 of 93 hours). The visual survey on the same cruise (CC0907) logged 19 blue whale sightings, more than any other cruise 2008-2010, so blue whales were there; the acoustic scoring appears to have skipped blue calls on CC0907MA.
